question.knowledge_point: Finding the First Term of an Arithmetic Series Given a Term and the Sum
question.problem: Find the first term of an arithmetic series if its $17$th term is $33$ and the sum of the first $30$ terms is $1\,080.$
question.worked_solution:
We are given one term of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=30$ and ${S}_{N}=1\,080$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 1\,080 & =\frac{30}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(30-1)d) \\ 1\,080 & =15(2{a}_{1}+29d) \\ \frac{1\,080}{15} & =2{a}_{1}+29d \\ 72 & =2{a}_{1}+29d.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we can write an equation for the $17$th term of the arithmetic series  and substitute in its known value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ {a}_{17} & ={a}_{1}+(17-1)d \\ 33 & ={a}_{1}+16d\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}33={a}_{1}+16d \\ 72=2{a}_{1}+29d\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and add the result to the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-66 & =-2{a}_{1}-32d \\ 72 & =2{a}_{1}+29d \\ 6 & =-3d \\ d & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $d=-2$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}33 & ={a}_{1}+16(-2) \\ 33 & ={a}_{1}-32 \\ {a}_{1} & =65.\end{aligned}
$$
